body: Deep semantic understanding of events requires recognizing related events and distinguishing why an event occurs from how it is carried out. 5W1H extraction provides a structured foundation for such understanding by organizing event information around six fundamental questions. However, single-event slot filling provides limited support for these distinctions. We propose ANCHOR, a cluster-grounded framework that combines a large language model (LLM) with a small language model equipped with discriminative heads for accurate 5W1H extraction. The LLM proposes candidate events and generates their initial 4W records, which guide the selection of an event cluster and the subsequent anchoring of its main event. A shared document encoder provides evidence for joint 4W refinement, and two separate sets of boundary and role-scoring heads then extract why and how under event-specific constraints, respectively. Document representations are reused across events and stages, and unsupported roles can remain empty. Following the same principles, an agent-and-skill annotation workflow constructs a benchmark of 26,110 documents from ten source corpora covering three languages and seven domains. We select nine of the resulting datasets to evaluate ANCHOR against strong baselines using four open-weight LLMs. ANCHOR achieves competitive performance. The datasets and code are available at https://github.com/revolution6575/ANCHOR-5W1H.
